name: turn-structure-v14
description: THE PAIRED CONTROL for the 19/08/2026 turn-structure change, and the one arm the plan says must be run before any buy/market code is deleted. It restores the turn as it stood the day before: the GBP 1 card buy back on, the GBP 3 market back on, the GBP 2 starter upgrade back to costing a whole MAIN ACTION, and the bonus slot takeable at any point in the turn rather than only at the start. Four rules, one arm, because all four move the same number - the visit rate - and measuring any of them alone reproduces a game nobody is proposing. THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES IT: the visit share of bonus slots, read off the five-way tally (visit-coin / visit-power / own-power / upgrade / SLOT UNSPENT). Two readings must not be misread. An upgrade spike in the opening rounds followed by a visit-heavy midgame is a PASS, not a fail - the upgrade is capped at three flips a seat and cannot crowd the visit out all game, which is the whole difference between it and the market it replaced. A rising SLOT UNSPENT share is the start-of-turn restriction biting, and it is a different disease from the market's: the visit is not being outcompeted, it is being missed. THE WARNING ON RECORD: the old no-coin-sinks arm (reports/watchlist-2026-08-04T21-37-21-reference-v8-no-coin-sinks.txt, n=1510) put visits at 0.40 per player per turn, a FAIL, against 0.54-0.56 PASS on same-day controls with both sinks in. That arm is from before the wild substitution, before Tier 3 became GROW and before these 31 cards, and critically it had neither the upgrade in the slot nor the start-of-turn restriction - so it is a warning, not a verdict. If the visit rate falls here, split the cause with bonus-any-time and upgrade-main-action, which arm the two halves separately.
